anchors.raw: I was quite 92 a year and a half ago. I got to 86, I think last year... And it was not me planning and setting, huh, I'll reduce this much weight. I was just consistent in what I'm doing. And that gradually showed up
anchors.note: The most powerful undercutting anchor available to any prospect: proof that the free, unstructured approach already works for him. Eight kilos lost with no coach, no plan and no cost. Unaddressed.

anchors.raw: alternatively I try to go for like 30-40 minutes at the gym
anchors.note: An existing gym habit plus 6,000-8,000 daily steps from work already occupies the activity slot at near-zero marginal cost. Never priced or contrasted.

unmet_demand.want: A low-commitment on-ramp — one or two 20-minute sessions a week to build confidence before scaling up
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme requires three to four days a week for six months and there is no smaller entry point; the rep stated the load as a qualifier and offered no alternative. The prospect described exactly the product he would buy and it does not exist.

unmet_demand.want: Something that survives a schedule with 4am starts, 2am finishes and weekly travel between three emirates
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. No flexibility, pause, or minimum-viable-week mechanism was described, and the only load statement made was a fixed frequency.

unmet_demand.want: Progress without goals or deadlines — 'I want to make it like a part of my lifestyle... without me focusing particularly on the end goal'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme's structure, the guarantee and the whole sales process are built on targets, weekly metrics and commitment framing. This is a genuine mismatch between what the buyer wants psychologically and how the product is built and sold.
